strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved scaling
strategies.desc: Uses 8 sequential all_reduce calls with interleaved element-wise scaling and unscaling operations between each stage. Total of 8 all_reduce dispatches plus local scaling ops. Straightforward translation of the problem statement with no fusion—trades simplicity for dispatch overhead.

strategies.name: Fused scaling within all-reduce loop
strategies.desc: Pre-computes scale/unscale coefficient products across stages and applies accumulated scaling factors, reducing intermediate clone() and scaling operations. Still requires 8 all_reduce dispatches but eliminates redundant buf allocations by reusing tensors. Reduces memory operations while keeping same collective count.

strategies.name: Vectorized per-shard scale application
strategies.desc: Pre-builds a scale tensor of shape (W*S,) containing replicated per-shard coefficients, enabling single broadcast multiply/divide instead of W-iteration loops. Maintains 8 all_reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead from O(W) loops to O(1) vectorized ops per stage. Better CPU/accelerator utilization on large world sizes.

strategies.name: Chunked reduce-scatter plus all-gather pattern
strategies.desc: Replaces monolithic all_reduce with reduce_scatter to distribute W shards across ranks, apply scaling locally on smaller chunks, then all_gather to reconstruct. For 8 stages: 8*(reduce_scatter + all_gather) = 16 dispatches, but each operates on S-sized chunks instead of W*S, reducing per-collective payload by factor of W. Exploits bandwidth-latency tradeoff at world_size=224.

strategies.name: Pipelined all-reduce with async dispatch
strategies.desc:
Splits the W*S tensor into multiple independent segments and issues overlapping all_reduce operations across stages where data dependencies permit (stages processing different shard-groups). Uses async collective launches to hide latency, potentially 8+ dispatches but with pipeline parallelism. Requires careful dependency tracking to respect scale/unscale ordering per shard.
